items.item_text: Graduation from high school or a General Education Diploma.
Bachelor of Science degree
Is exposed to marked changes in temperature and/or humidity: Yes
Dust: Yes
Fumes: Yes
Minimum of 2 years of college education or laboratory working experience
Minimum of 0.5 years of experience working in nematology or microbiology laboratory

Assist with suppressive soil screening experiment by conducting cyst nematode pot experiment with cabbage in quarantine greenhouse, under close supervision. The cabbage seedlings will be inoculated with cyst nematodes juveniles. After several nematode generations of culture, the female and cyst stage of the nematodes will be collected from the pots using power wash system in greenhouse, and be counted using a microscope, a pair of forceps, a balance, and a clicker counter. The data will be recorded in the data sheet and entered in the computer later. Nematode and rhizosphere soil samples will be preserved for later experiment use and for necessary genetic analysis. (30% time)

Assist with microbial RT-PCR assay development, under close supervision. These work would require following multiple modified manufactured manuals of commercial kits and established operation protocols to conduct DNA/RNA extraction, gel electrophoresis analysis, fluorescence reading analysis, cDNA synthesis, and RT-PCR analysis. (25% time)

Assist with plant nematode behavior plate assays, under close supervision. These assays would include nematode sterilization and observation of nematode behaviors in Petri dishes and glass discs using a microscope, camera, tally counter and computers. The work would require following established operation protocols. (20% time)

Maintain plant, nematode, fungi and bacteria cultures. The work includes clean containers, germinate and transplant seedlings, prepare planting materials, prepare culture media and plates, set up planting pots, water plants, fertilize plants, trim plant tissues, inoculate plants with nematodes, and subculture nematode and microbial cultures routinely. (15% time)

General laboratory maintenance by using laboratory sink, greenhouse sink, bleach and other detergents, rinsing all containers, equipment that are used for nematode extraction, nematode or microbial counting, plant culture, and microbial culture. (10% time)
